A central heating project should start with the rooms you use and the system already in place.

PLAN THE WORK

Make the system fit the home.

An extension, a changed floor plan or a different use for a room can alter its heating needs. Share plans and room dimensions alongside details of the current boiler and radiators.

Agree whether the work involves individual components or a wider system change. Pipe routes, floor access, controls and the sequence of other renovation work can all affect the installation.

Ask how the completed work will be checked and explained at handover. Understanding your controls is part of making the most of the system.

THINGS TO DISCUSS

Make the brief clear.

  • Existing heating system assessment
  • Radiator and pipework requirements
  • Controls and room-by-room use
  • Installation scope and access

GOOD TO KNOW

Your questions,
answered.

Will a bigger boiler solve cold rooms?

Not necessarily. Radiator sizing, circulation, controls and the building itself can affect comfort. Discuss the whole system before replacing components.
